summary: Validated cursor + wake lock fixes in /app/frontend/public/cliente.js via Playwright with getDisplayMedia and navigator.wakeLock stubs installed via add_init_script BEFORE navigation. 3 of 4 requested scenarios PASS. 1 scenario (re-acquisition on visibilitychange) FAILS due to a real logic bug in the fix: the closure variable `wakeLock` is never nulled when the browser auto-releases the sentinel while the tab is hidden, so the guard `!wakeLock` in the visibilitychange listener is always false and re-acquisition never fires. Regression flow (tecnico login + btn-ver -> video-ecra.srcObject non-null + #video-espera oculto) still works.

integration_issues.flow: Screen Wake Lock re-acquisition after tab visibility returns
integration_issues.issue: In cliente.js the visibilitychange listener guards with `!wakeLock` but wakeLock is only ever nulled inside libertarWakeLock() (called on parar). When the browser auto-releases the sentinel while the tab is hidden, the JS reference is NOT touched, so on `visibilitychange -> visible` the guard `!wakeLock` is false and navigator.wakeLock.request('screen') is NEVER called again. Confirmed: after dispatching visibilitychange hidden then visible with an active stream, window.__wakeCalls.length remained at 1 (only the initial call).

action_items: Fix wake lock re-acquisition: inside pedirWakeLock(), change the empty release listener to also null the closure var. E.g. `wakeLock.addEventListener('release', () => { wakeLock = null; });`. This lets the existing visibilitychange listener re-request when the tab becomes visible again. Without this the reported bug #1 (screen turns off, share stops) is only partially mitigated — the initial request works, but the automatic re-acquire path is dead code.
critical_code_review_comments: cliente.js line 96: `wakeLock.addEventListener('release', () => {});` is a no-op. It MUST set `wakeLock = null` so that the visibilitychange re-acquire branch (line 107 `!wakeLock`) can ever be true.

getDisplayMedia constraint `video.cursor: 'always'` is deprecated in newer specs (replaced by `preferCurrentTab`/`surfaceSwitching`/`selfBrowserSurface`, and cursor via `displaySurface` hints). Chromium still accepts it as a legacy hint, so it works today, but consider adding `{ cursor: 'always' }` as a MediaTrackConstraints on the track (applyConstraints) too for future-proofing.

Wake Lock in a hidden tab is impossible by spec — this cannot fix the case where the OS itself sleeps (only the display staying on while tab is visible). Consider also playing a tiny silent looping audio to keep the tab active on some platforms, or a NoSleep.js fallback for iOS Safari (where wakeLock is unsupported).

cliente.js has no try/catch around addEventListener('release',...) — safe today, but if wakeLock.request returns non-standard object on older browsers it could throw before the sentinel is stored. Not a critical bug.

rca of the issue: In cliente.js pedirWakeLock() stores the sentinel in the closure variable `wakeLock` and attaches an empty release listener. When the tab is hidden the User Agent auto-releases the sentinel and fires the release event, but the JS reference `wakeLock` remains truthy. The visibilitychange listener re-acquires only when `!wakeLock`, so it never fires. Fix: in the release listener, `wakeLock = null;`. Reproduction: open cliente.html, click cliente-comecar-btn, dispatch visibilitychange twice (hidden then visible). Observe window.__wakeCalls length stays 1.
